t.6.1.1: Having heard the words of Hanumān, spoken exactly as they should be, Rāma, filled with joy, spoke these words in reply.
t.6.1.2: A very great deed, hard to accomplish on earth, has been done by Hanumān, a deed that no one else on the face of the earth could achieve even in thought.
t.6.1.3: Indeed, I see no one who could cross the great ocean, apart from Garuḍa and Vāyu, and apart from Hanumān.
t.6.1.4: the city of Laṅkā, well guarded by Rāvaṇa, unassailable by Devas, Dānavas and Yakṣas, by Gandharvas, Uragas and Rākṣasas.
t.6.1.5: Having entered it relying on his own courage, who indeed could come out alive? Who could enter that city, so very hard to assail and well guarded by the rākṣasas, unless, endowed with valor and strength, he were an equal of Hanumān?
t.6.1.6: A great servant's duty to Sugrīva has been performed by Hanumān, who thus put forth his own strength in a manner befitting his valor.
t.6.1.7: A servant who, being appointed by his master to a difficult task, performs it with devotion to him, him they call the best of men.
t.6.1.8: A servant who, though appointed by the king, capable, fit for the task and attentive, does not carry out the king's work, him they call the lowest of men.
t.6.1.9: Appointed to that task, Hanūmān has accomplished what had to be done; he has not let himself be diminished, and Sugrīva too has been pleased.
t.6.1.10: I, the race of Raghu, and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa have today been rightly protected, in accordance with dharma, through the finding of Vaidehī.
t.6.1.11: But this torments my mind all the more, wretched as I am: that here I can do no kindness worthy of him who has brought me such welcome news.
t.6.1.12: But this embrace, which is all I have to give, has been bestowed by me, now that this moment has come, upon that great-souled Hanumān.
t.6.1.13: The search for Sītā has indeed been accomplished well in every way; but on reaching the ocean, my mind is once again lost in despair.
t.6.1.14: How indeed will the monkeys, gathered together, reach the southern shore of the ocean, so hard to cross, with its mighty waters?
t.6.1.15: Although this news of Vaidehī has been told to me, what answer can there be to the monkeys' crossing to the far shore of the ocean?
t.6.1.16: Having spoken thus to Hanūmān, the mighty-armed Rāma, slayer of enemies, bewildered with grief, then fell into deep thought.
